bridges.claim: Conscious states have properties, unity, and intentional content that cannot be reduced to physical brain states.
An indivisible, enduring subject is needed to ground personhood and identity through physical change.
Libertarian agency and rational deliberation require a nonphysical personal originator.
Functional dependence on the brain is compatible with a soul that interacts with and acts through the body.

routes.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
routes.position: No soul has been shown to exist

bridges.claim: No soul has been reliably demonstrated.
A proposed soul requires a reliable way to distinguish it from unsupported or merely sufficient explanations.
Observed mental attributes vary with brain structure and function, supporting brain-dependent accounts.
Physical or emergent accounts remain live alternatives, so unexplained consciousness does not establish a soul.
Continuing personal identity can reflect practical human labeling amid ongoing physical and experiential change.
